text:
Two seasons ago Sergei Murashov was stopping pucks for the Wheeling Nailers in the ECHL. On Wednesday in San Jose he was the reason the Penguins left with two points, a 3-2 shootout win that never felt as comfortable as the 2-0 lead suggested.

Pittsburgh had the better of it early. The Penguins out-chanced the Sharks 1.31 to 0.57 in expected goals (the quality of chances) in the first period, and Samuel Girard put them ahead at 8:57 with a slap shot that had about a 6% chance of going in, set up by Evgeni Malkin and Kris Letang. Ben Kindel made it 2-0 on the power play 3:28 into the third, and our win probability had Pittsburgh at 92%.

Then the Sharks' kids took over. Macklin Celebrini scored at 11:32 for his 200th career point, and four minutes later he set up Mason Marchment, whose 100th career goal tied it at 15:49. That goal moved San Jose from a 12% chance to 52%, the biggest swing of the night. Overtime belonged to the Sharks (0.73 expected goals to 0.15), and Murashov's stop on Will Smith was the save of the game. Over the night he made 34 saves on 36 shots and saved 1.4 goals more than those shots deserved. Yaroslav Askarov was nearly as good at the other end, 33 of 35. Kindel scored the only goal of the shootout.

By the numbers this was a coin flip: 3.34 expected goals for Pittsburgh, 3.39 for San Jose, and the Sharks deserved to win 51% of replays. The Sharks went 0 for 5 on the power play despite 1.27 expected goals on it, which is where the game slipped away from them.

For Pittsburgh, the points matter less than the backdrop. The headlines this week are about whether a struggling team starts selling, and what that means for Malkin, Erik Karlsson and a 39-year-old Sidney Crosby in the last year of his contract. Nights like this, decided by a young goalie and a shootout, won't settle that argument either way.
headline: Murashov holds the fort as the Sharks' kids rally
